metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 24 Outward Return Movement Pairs
metadata.dataset_description: Paired outward and return Montréal movements with shared pair IDs, reversed endpoints, activity stays, modes, route directness, point speeds, and return intervals.
metadata.metric_note: Distances and directness are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; point speeds, trip durations, chain timing, and paired-leg timing are synchronized with the supplied point table. Route directness ratio is route distance divided by straight-line distance, so it is at least 1 and lower values indicate more direct routes.

plot.title: Mode, Route, and Speed within Pairs
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Do outward and return legs preserve mode while differing in route directness and speed profile?
insight_list.insight: Outbound and return legs usually preserve transport mode, but often differ in route directness and speed profiles.

plot.title: Destination-stay Duration by Activity
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do work, shopping, dining, and leisure pairs differ in destination-stay duration?
insight_list.insight: Work-based pairs have longer and more regular destination stays, while shopping and dining pairs show shorter and more variable activity intervals.

plot.title: Stay Duration and Return-mode Change
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Are longer destination stays more likely to be followed by a mode change?
insight_list.insight: Pairs with longer destination stays are more likely to change transport mode on the return leg, especially for leisure-related trips.

plot.title: Outward Time and Return Interval
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How does outward departure period relate to the interval before return?
insight_list.insight: Morning outward trips are commonly paired with evening returns, while midday outward trips tend to have much shorter return intervals.

insights: Outbound and return legs usually preserve transport mode, but often differ in route directness and speed profiles.
Work-based pairs have longer and more regular destination stays, while shopping and dining pairs show shorter and more variable activity intervals.
Pairs with longer destination stays are more likely to change transport mode on the return leg, especially for leisure-related trips.
Morning outward trips are commonly paired with evening returns, while midday outward trips tend to have much shorter return intervals.
summary: Outward and return legs usually preserve mode but differ in geometry and speed shape. Work stays are long and regular; shopping and dining stays are shorter and variable. Longer stays, particularly leisure stays, have more return-mode changes, while morning departures have the longest return intervals.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
